title: Questions to Ask About a Gluten-Free Event Menu
body_html:
A gluten-free event menu requires clear ingredient and preparation questions. Explain each guest’s requirements and ask the provider about feasible controls, labels and cross-contact limitations.

For the service options, explore catering services in Dubai. Use this guide to prepare the details for your enquiry.

Explain the guest requirements clearly

Tell the provider which guests require gluten-free food and whether they have coeliac disease, a wheat allergy or another requirement. These should not be treated as interchangeable. Follow the guest’s or their clinician’s instructions rather than assuming that a menu label alone answers the brief.

Ask about every component

Discuss sauces, dressings, stocks, coatings, garnishes and bought-in ingredients as well as the main dishes. Ask how ingredient information is checked and how substitutions will be communicated before service. Keep the approved menu and dietary notes together.

Discuss preparation and cross-contact limits

Ask about preparation surfaces, utensils, storage and cooking equipment. The provider should explain what separation is feasible and what limitations remain. A private kitchen, a production kitchen and a buffet have different practical constraints; none should be described as risk-free without evidence.

Plan labels and serving responsibilities

Agree how the required meals will be identified and handed to the correct guests. Ask who answers ingredient questions during service and how serving utensils will be managed. Avoid expecting guests to make decisions from the appearance of a dish.

Compare scope rather than rankings

Assess each proposal against the same written requirements. A claim to be the best gluten-free caterer is less useful than a clear explanation of ingredients, preparation and service. Do not rely on unsupported ratings or assume that a dietary request can always be accommodated.

Confirm feasibility before booking

Explore allergy-aware catering and dietary planning and ask the team to assess the requirements. The written response should identify the agreed menu and any limitations before the booking is confirmed.
